previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with tarry stools, coffee-ground emesis, and abdominal pain, one week after a prior admission with similar symptoms. She reported lightheadedness, palpitations, and two episodes of red urine, which had never occurred before. Her hemoglobin remained stable during admission, and rectal exam was guaiac negative. An endoscopy from the previous admission was normal, so no further invasive procedures were performed. She was managed supportively with IV fluids, pantoprazole, and sucralfate, with transition to oral intake and pain control. H. pylori antibody was positive, but treatment was deferred given lack of active ulceration. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home on hospital day four, tolerating oral intake and ambulating. The cause of her abdominal pain and gastrointestinal symptoms remained unclear, possibly self-limited or related to her complex medical history. Follow-up with gastroenterology and rheumatology was advised, along with consideration of pain psychology for chronic pain management.
